title: Developer experience: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs site ops, top support issues and canonical fixes
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This living guide describes the standards, templates, quickstarts, and operating procedures used by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team to produce SDK guides, API examples, quickstarts, and canonical support fixes. The goal is consistency, fast onboarding for new users, and a single source of truth for common issues and their resolutions.

Scope:
- SDK guides (Python, Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and templated projects
- API examples and copy/paste snippets for docs and blog posts
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, review, metrics)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained in a single KB

Audience:
Primary: developer-facing engineers, technical writers, solutions engineers, support engineers. Secondary: product and sales engineers who reuse examples.

1) Ownership and responsibilities
- Owner: DevEx (engineering) — contact: devex@redwood.ai
- Doc steward (updates & metrics): Ava Martinez
- Release / publish approver: Maya Chen (content lead)
- Support canonical fix owner: Support rotation (see runbook)

2) Document structure conventions (required)
- Title: short, descriptive, dashed file name for exports (e.g. "sdk-python-quickstart-2026.json").
- Intro: 2–4 sentence summary + audience + prerequisites.
- Getting started: Minimal runnable example with copy/paste commands.
- Reference: complete API surface links and common options (timeouts, retries, streaming).
- Troubleshooting: top issues and diagnostics.
- Changelog: date + owner + summary of change.

3) Templates (canonical files provided in the repo)
Available templates (repo: github.com/redwood/devex-templates):
- minimal-quickstart-python: CLI + pip, 2-file example, 30s run time
- minimal-quickstart-node: npm + single file example
- app-template-react-chat: front-end chat UI wired to sandbox API key
- server-template-go: example for embedding pipelines and batching

Template required files:
| file | purpose | notes |
|---|---|---|
| README.md | description + prerequisites | Must include expected output sample |
| .env.example | example env var names | DO NOT include real keys |
| quickstart.sh | bootstrap script | installs deps, runs smoke test |
| example-config.yaml | default client config | explain timeout, batch_size, model |

Naming/labels for templates:
- Use semantic versioning in template metadata: v1.0.0
- Labels: sdk, quickstart, template, language-[python|node|go|java]

4) SDK guide standards (per-language)
General rules:
- Provide a 1-minute quickstart at top (copy/paste).
- Show auth patterns (API key + env var injection) and best practices for KMS/HSM in Private deployments.
- Include streaming examples and error handling.
- Each SDK guide must include a small benchmark for cold-start call latency (median, p95) for the sample payload.

Python (required sections):
- pip install, client instantiation, sync/async examples, streaming, function calling, structured output parsing.
- Code example header must include tested SDK version (e.g., redwood==0.6.3).

Node (required):
- npm/yarn install, ESM and CommonJS examples, streaming via EventSource or fetch, serverless usage notes.

Go (required):
- go get instructions, context cancellation example, connection pooling best practices.

5) API examples (copy/paste ready)
Include three canonical examples in each SDK page:
- Simple completion (prompt -> text)
- Chat with system + user messages, tool calling stub
- Embeddings example (cosine similarity quick demo)

Example: Python completion (1-minute quickstart)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate(text="Translate the following to French: 'Hello team'", model="redwood-1-small")
print(resp.text)
```

Example: Node chat streaming (abridged)
```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1-small', messages: [{role: 'system', content: 'You are concise.'}, {role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the release notes.'}] })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```

6) Docs site operating procedures (publish workflow)
Publishing steps (authors must follow):
1. Draft in branch: create feature branch docs/<short-name>.
2. Internal review: assign 2 reviewers from DevEx or content team. Use PR template "doc-change".
3. Blockers: performance-sensitive examples must include benchmark results.
4. Merge: author adds changelog entry in the doc header.
5. Staging deploy: docs-staging.redwood.ai — smoke test quickstart (run quickstart.sh).
6. Production deploy: scheduled daily at 03:00 UTC or manual for urgent fixes.
7. Post-publish: update metrics dashboard and Slack #docs-notify channel.

Required checks on PRs:
- Linter: markdownlint and code sample runner (pytest for python snippets).
- Accessibility: alt text for images and code block labels.
- Security: verify no real credentials in snippets.

Metrics & quality SLOs (tracked weekly):
- Time-to-first-fix (TTFF) for docs bugs: target <= 72 hours
- Docs test pass rate for samples: >= 95%
- Page satisfaction (thumbs-up/down): target > 90% positive

7) Support escalation & canonical fixes (procedure)
When a support issue is triaged and appears >3x in 7 days or affects >2 customers, create a canonical fix doc using this template and link it in KB: steps.
Steps to create a canonical fix:
1. Reproduce: reproduce the customer issue in a sandbox. Record request id and logs.
2. Root cause analysis: document the fault (bug, auth, misconfiguration, model mismatch).
3. Fix: include code/CLI commands and recommended config changes.
4. Validation: run smoke tests and monitor for recurrence for 48 hours.
5. Publish: add to support KB and link to SDK guide's troubleshooting section.
6. Communicate: post in #support and notify affected customers via CS.

Top support issues (current canonical list)
- AUTH_INVALID_KEY (auth / tokens)
  - Symptom: 401 responses with "invalid api key".
  - Root cause: rotated key or missing "REDWOOD_API_KEY" in environment.
  - Fix: rotate key, update .env and restart service. CLI to test: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models`
- RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (rate limiting)
  - Symptom: 429 responses for burst traffic.
  - Root cause: single-client burst; no exponential backoff.
  - Fix: implement exponential backoff (retry-after header), use batching or dedicated capacity for high throughput.
- STREAM_TIMEOUT (streaming disconnects)
  - Symptom: partial responses, closed connection during streaming.
  - Root cause: intermediate proxies or client read timeout < server keep-alive.
  - Fix: increase client read timeout to 120s, ensure proxy keep-alive enabled. Example Node config: `fetch(url, { timeout: 120000 })`.
- MODEL_MISMATCH (model variant / API surface mismatch)
  - Symptom: SDK call fails with unknown param or unexpected output shape.
  - Root cause: server-side rollout of model variant or client pinned to older SDK.
  - Fix: upgrade SDK to supported version, or pin model to compatible variant in request.
- EMBEDDING_DIM_MISMATCH (embeddings)
  - Symptom: similarity calculations fail or produce NaNs.
  - Root cause: comparing embeddings from different models or using different normalization.
  - Fix: ensure same model used for both vectors; document expected dimension in SDK guide and provide normalization helper snippet.

Example canonical fix (abridged)
Title: "Auth: 401 after key rotation"
Summary: Customer rotated keys during maintenance and did not update deployment secrets.
Resolution steps:
1. Identify affected services via logs (filter: "401 Authorization").
2. Update secrets manager with new key.
3. Restart service or trigger seamless secret reload.
4. Validate with `/v1/models` curl check.

8) Troubleshooting checklist (for oncall & support)
- Verify network: traceroute, curl to api.redwood.ai
- Verify auth: print env var or secrets manager value (do not log keys)
- Verify SDK version: `pip show redwood` or `npm ls redwood-sdk`
- Verify model name & params: ensure model exists in model catalog and client supports the parameters used
- Check quota & rate limits: billing console / usage dashboard

9) Maintenance & cadence
- Quarterly reviews: update quickstarts and SDK samples for breaking API changes or new popular models.
- Post-incident update: any incident that leads to a public-facing bug must generate an updated quickstart within 7 days.
- Template rotation: deprecate templates older than 18 months or when dependent on deprecated SDKs.

10) Appendix: useful commands & scripts
- Smoke test quickstart (bash):
  - `./quickstart.sh` (must exit 0 and print "smoke test passed")
- Validate python snippets (local):
  - `python -m pytest tests/snippets_test.py`
- Check docs staging URL: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/<path>
